contexts.text: That the Lord foresaw that He could thus save the human race. Signified, Explained.
Unless the Lord had reduced the human race into this genius, or state (of the Church called Noah), no man could ever have been saved.
Who would save the universal human race.
If only Divine truth (were predicated of the Lord) no mortal could be saved.
Love Itself... wills to save all. AC 1803.
He willed to be made certain that the human race would be saved. Signified.
The salvation of the human race was His only consolation.
For the salvation (of the universal human race). He fought in all His temptations.
Therefore He is so often called, in the Old Testament the Saviour, etc., which is His name Jesus.
That everyone who should... love Him, and the things which are of Him, and should be in His love which is towards the universal human race... should be conjoined and saved.
This (life of charity) is the life which saves after death, and never any life of faith without it. Explained.
The Angels, to save a soul from Hell, regard death as nothing, and would, if possible, undergo Hell.
The gentiles... are equally saved, when they are rational, that is, live in charity.
It is true that those who have faith are saved. (Explained.)
Believe that they are saved of the Lord's mercy only.
(The Lord) obtained that those might be saved with whom there are goods and truths. AC 2141.
Thus was made known to Him... the quality of the human race which would be saved through Him, that is, through the union of the Human essence with the Divine, in Him. AC 2218:2.
That by Him all who are in charity will be saved. Signified, Explained.

Those who are gifted with goods... are also gifted with eternal salvation, that is, are saved. All the nations of the earth = those in goods... not all the people in the world... because very many among them are not saved: only those in charity.

By (mere thought, the acknowledgement of something to be believed, or the Knowledge of all things of the doctrine of faith) no one can be saved; for they cannot send a root any deeper than into the thought. Thought saves no one; but it is the life which he has procured to himself in the world through the Knowledges of faith...
He who believes... that any man can save, and therefore worships him, from this falsity does evil.
From doctrine, they say that the Lord is the Saviour of the human face... yet few believe it.
In His state of glorification... the Lord does not intercede, but... from His Divine bears aid, and saves.
The universal human race, which He burned to save to eternity.

It may be supposed that man cannot but be saved if his truths are full of goods; but (still) he is saved... from mercy; for there are very few truths with man, and the goods in them have their quality according to the truths and life of the man. Explained.
[Five classes of those who] will be saved. Signified. AC 2273. AC 2277. AC 2281. AC 2285.
Not that they would be saved on account of temptations; for some undergo temptations who succumb... Nay, neither is man saved on account of temptations, if he places anything of merit in them...

They judge that (others) cannot be saved unless they believe as they do, which the Lord forbade (). From much experience (I know) that men are saved from every religion, provided that through a life of charity they have received remains of good and appearances of truth. This is meant by, I will not destroy (Sodom) for ten's sake, by which is signified that if there were remains they would be saved.

The life of charity is... to perceive joy from the fact that others also are saved; but those have not the life of charity who wish that no others be saved than those who believe as they do: this may be evident from the mere fact that more from the gentiles, than from Christians, are saved.
It now follows concerning the salvation of those who are in some good and truth, who, in this chapter, are represented by Lot.
In this chapter it treats of Judgment; namely, of the Salvation of the faithful, and the damnation of the unfaithful.

In all temptation there is doubt about Salvation, etc. (in order that) they may be confirmed in the fact that all things are of the Lord's mercy; that they are saved through Him alone; and that with themselves there is nothing but evil.

To be judged from good, is to be saved, because they have received it... Good is the Lord's; and they who acknowledge this in life and faith, are the lord's, and therefore are saved; but they who do not acknowledge it in life... cannot be the Lord's, thus cannot be saved. Explained.
That all in the good of charity... would be saved; and also those in the truth of faith, if they would recede from evil. Signified, Explained.
(Thus) man cannot be saved through (merely) thinking and speaking truth, or even good.
That those in the affection of truth, that is, in faith, are saved, provided it is the faith of good.

God remembered Abraham = salvation through the unition of the Lord's Divine essence with His Human essence; and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow = the salvation of those who are in good, and of those who are in truth in which is good... the cities in which Lot dwelt = although they who were saved were also in falsities from evils. AC 2457.
After the fall... the human race of that time could not have been saved (without these representations before the Angels).
See Gentile. AC 2590, etc.

The Lord did not come... to save the celestial, but the spiritual. If the Most Ancient Church... had remained in its integrity, the Lord would have had no need to be born a man... Those of the Ancient Church (being spiritual) could not have been saved unless the Lord had come into the world. Signified.
With the Lord, when He was in the world, were represented all the states of the Church, and how they would be saved through Him.
In no other way (than by the separation from Him of the merely human Rational) could the human race be saved.
Preface. Those who arrogate to themselves the Power of saving the human race...
() treats of the salvation of those who constitute the Lord's Spiritual Church, through this union. AC 2765.
From good is all deliverance and Salvation. Truth condemns and good saves. References.
Thine only one, whom thou lovest = the only thing (the Human) in the universe, by which He would save the human race. Explained.
It is this union (the Divine Human) through which can be saved those who have the faith of charity in Him; for the Supreme Divine Itself could no longer reach the human race...

If the Lord had not united (the two Essences, neither men nor the spiritual Angels) would have had any capacity for understanding truth and good; thus would have had nothing of blessedness, and consequently nothing of salvation; from which it is evident that the human race could not have been saved, unless the Lord had assumed the Human...
(The notion that) men are saved if they only think from a kind of interior emotion that the Lord suffered for them...
That the spiritual are saved through charity, and not through faith separated from charity. Signified, Explained.
The Salvation of all who are in good. Signified, Explained.
In these words is contained this arcanum: that through the Church are saved those outside the Church. (Explained.)
As in () it has treated of those who are saved by the Lord's Divine Human within the Church; in what follows, to the end of the chapter, it treats of those who are saved outside the Church.
These constitute the third class of the spiritual who are saved. Signified.
If man could be reformed under compulsion, there would be no man in the universe who was not saved...
Our Saviour was called Lord... because He was Jehovah.
Under Redeem, see this reference.
The reason Jesus = Divine good, is that it means salvation, Salvation, and Saviour; for from the Divine good... and thus through the reception of it, is all Salvation.
By the 12 thousand sealed from every tribe, is signified that all in faith, that is, in its good, are saved.
That by the good and truth which are from the Lord, are saved all who live in mutual charity, whether within or without the Church. Signified.
Through (the Divine Human) man is saved; for unless... man could mentally view and adore the Lord's Human, and thus have access to the Divine, he could never have been saved.
He that persevereth unto the end, he shall be saved () = the Salvation of those in charity.
(Thus) works are what save man, and what condemn him... for in works is man's will... Illustrated.
Believes that... he can be saved by faith, however he has lived...
(Joseph)... in the external sense, = Salvation...
I will save the house of Joseph... ()... treats of the Salvation of the Spiritual.

(Although man has few genuine truths) still, those in the good of life are saved. The reason they can be saved, is that the Lord's Divine is in (this good); and, where that is, all things are disposed into order, so that they can be conjoined with the genuine goods and genuine truths which are in the Heavens.
Under Believe, see this reference.
In every doctrine are some who are saved.

He who does not know that... no regeneration is possible except in freedom, when he reasons about... the Salvation of man... casts himself into mere shades... supposing that if the Lord willed. He could save everyone, by innumerable means. Enumerated.
For everyone (even the most external) who is in a life of good from the affection of charity, is saved.
For whatever inflows from the Lord is an end which regards the Salvation of the human race.
They are ignorant that it is what is internal which saves or damns; and not what is external separated from what is internal.
Two shall be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left = that those (in the Church) who are in good will be saved; and those in evil damned.

As men hae made faith (alone) saving; yet see that the truths of faith cannot save, because they exist with the evil also, they acknowledge confidence... If the confidence which appears in a state of compulsion would save man, all mortals would be saved: for everyone is easily reduced to it.
Hamor and Shechem, with their families (were killed) that they might be saved.
This is why, if the natural man has not been prepared (here) to receive the truths and goods of faith, he cannot receive them (there), thus cannot be saved...
But, in the Divine affection, there is the end for the sake of self... to save the human race. Illustrated.

In order that those of the Spiritual Church could be saved, the Lord miraculously separated their intellectual part from their voluntary, and implanted in the intellectual the power to receive a new Voluntary. References.
All those virgins... trimmed their lamps... For, those in truths (alone)... suppose that faith alone saves, not knowing that there is no faith where there is no charity.
They preach... faith alone, and say it is saving without works.
The savingness of faith they place in confidence... and even persuade that the confidence of one moment... saves. AC 4925:2.
They who live a life of faith, adore the Lord... as God the Saviour.
That no one can be saved unless he has lived in the good of charity. From experience.
If Heaven were of mercy or grace, independently of the life, everyone would be saved.
Consequently, all who have had conscience are saved; but those who have had none cannot be saved.
For, in order that man may be saved, he must be in freedom; and, in freedom, be withdrawn from evil, and be led to good. Explained.
This conscience (of what is just and fair) exists at this day with many; an interior conscience with few; but still those who enjoy the former conscience are saved in the other life...
From this it resulted that none but the celestial could then be saved; and, at last, scarcely these, unless the Lord had assumed the Human...
Unless the Divine Providence were in every most minute particular, man could not possibly be saved...
For the Lord loves the universal human race, and wills to save everyone to eternity.
Believe that Salvation is only introduction into Heaven of mercy... If (this were so) all in the whole world would be saved; for the lord... wills the salvation of all...
The sphere (which is about everyone from Heaven) is one of endeavours to do good, and save.

Such spiritual ones have been saved solely through the Lord's advent into the world: because the Divine passing through Heaven, which was the Divine Human (then), could not reach them. Explained. AC 7035:end.

By these judgments (or truths) those in falsities from evil are damned, and those in truths from good are saved... Nor do the truths which proceed from the Lord save, if the man believes that he is saved by the truths of faith with him, and not by mercy...

Those (of the savages in Venus) who are such that they can be saved, are in the places of vastation. Described... When they have suffered the extreme things, as the corporeal things with them have as it were died, they are finally saved.
He who believes that faith alone saves, and that works of charity contribute nothing to salvation; and also he who believes that he is saved even in the last hour...
For the end of order is Salvation; thus is to do good to all.
Truth is falsified when it is said that... thus man can be saved whatever his life may be; and (also) when it is said that no one is saved except those within the Church.
Unless (the Nephilim had been shut up by the Lord when He was in the world) very few could have been saved. Explained.
Natural good saves none; but spiritual good saves all. Explained.
Without the advent of the Lord into the world (those in the Lower Earth) could not possibly have been saved.
That the glorification and resurrection of the Lord as to His Human, is the source of all Salvation. Signified, Explained.
That in the minds of those (of the Spiritual Church) must be fixed this truth: that their salvation... is due to the Lord alone...
The reason falsity is not appropriated to him who is in good... is that he thinks well about God, etc... Unless this were the case, scarcely anyone could be saved...
A state of... the destruction of those in falsity from evil; and one of... the Salvation of those in truth from good. Signified, Explained.
Jehovah saved Israel () = that the Lord protected those of the Spiritual Church.
Under Mercy, see this reference.
That thus, without danger of infestation, all will be saved who are in the faculty of receiving the truth of good and the good of truth. Signified, Explained.
For, so long as the evil had not been cast into Hell, scarcely any could pass over, that is, be saved. Explained.

As it is charity which gives (the above-named) faculty, it is charity which saves; for those who are saved, are not saved through charity from themselves, but through charity from the Lord, consequently through this faculty of receiving.
He who wants to be saved, must confess his sins, and perform repentance. Explained.
The Salvation of the faithful. Ti.
(The inhabitants of Jupiter) do not worship the Lord as a King; but as a Saviour.
This order (of life) with man must be completely inverted in order for him to be saved; which is done through regeneration...
By the Divine remembrance is signified Salvation; and by oblivion, damnation.
Therefore, if these (Genii) were to inflow, the man of the Spiritual Church could never be saved. Explained.

It is according to order that those who have lived well are saved; and those who have lived evilly condemned... consequently, it is impossible for those in Hell to be brought out thence into Heaven, and saved of the Lord's pure mercy; for it is the reception of His mercy, when He lived (here), through which everyone is saved...

(There) all are consociated according to their life... hence it is not possible for the evil and the good to be together; nor is it possible for those to be in good who are evil; for good and evil are opposites, and the one destroys the other: (thus) it is not possible that those in Hell should be saved; thus it is not feasible that Salvation, however a man had lived, should be from mercy alone.
The Salvation of those who are of the external and internal Spiritual Church. Signified, Explained.

Those who have not received conscience (here), cannot receive it (there), thus cannot be saved, because they have no plane into which Heaven may inflow and operate, that is, the Lord through Heaven, and lead them to Himself.
Those in genuine truths are often damned; and those... in falsities are often saved. From experience.
To believe in God is the faith which saves; but to believe the things which are from God, is the faith, which, without the former one, does not save. Explained.
All who are in heavenly love have confidence that they will be saved by the Lord...
To believe the things which the Word, or doctrine, teaches, and not to live according to them, appears like faith... but by this alone no one is saved; for it is a persuasive faith.
(Thus) it is his own fault that he cannot be saved.
No one could have been saved. DLord 3:2.
From Divine power thus acquired in the Human, the Lord alone fights for... the universal human race, conquers, and thus saves.
Called Jesus, or Saviour, when good is treated of.
The priesthood, in the supreme sense, = the whole office which the Lord discharges as the Saviour; and whatever He performs as the Saviour, is from the Divine love...
By Aaron's office was represented all the work of Salvation...
The Lord as to the work of Salvation in successive order. Signified, Explained.
See Priest. AC 10017:2. AC 10152. AC 10279.

(Thus) was represented... the Divine power of saving the human race; and the power of saving the human race is power over the Heavens and Hells; for through this power... the Lord saves man. Explained.
Man is saved through the removal of evils and falsities from the Hells, and the influx, then, of the good of love and truth of faith through Heaven from the Lord.
The reason (the Lord so often said that the sick must have faith) was that the first thing of all is to acknowledge that the Lord is the Saviour of the world. (Explained.)

Those born within the Church who at heart deny the Lord, whatever may be their quality in moral life... cannot be saved. Illustrated. Whereas the gentiles who... have lived in some kind of charity towards their neighbour, and in some kind of love to God the Creator of the universe under a human form, in the other life are accepted by the Lord and saved; for, when instructed... they acknowledge the Lord, and believe in, and love Him.
The Lord's work of Salvation. Explained.
How man has been saved and redeemed by the Lord, through His subjugating the Hells, and glorifying His Human. Explained. AC 10828.
If not led through his Intellectual, no man could be saved.
Hence it is that everyone, from every religion, can be saved...
All would (then) be saved. HH 524.
Therefore such cannot be saved; for they have not Heaven in them.
Everyone with whom the Church is, is saved; but everyone with whom the Church is not, is condemned.
That those are saved who receive the Lord, and believe in Him; but not those in evils and the derivative falsities. Illustrated.
That the Gentiles also are saved, may be known from this alone: that the Lord's mercy is universal... HH 319, Explained.
A moral life for the sake of the Divine... saves man; (but a moral life for the sake of men in the world) does not save him. Explained.

The Divine mercy is pure mercy towards ail the human race to save it... and therefore everyone who can be saved, is saved; but no one can be saved except through Divine means... which are called Divine truths: these teach how man should live in order that he may be saved. Explained.

The Divine sphere proceeding from the Lord, is a perpetual endeavour of saving all; and, as those in the Hells cannot be saved, because all there are in evil, and against the Divine of the Lord, the... cruelties there are restrained so far as possible...
And when man's freedom perishes, he can no longer be saved. Explained.
On the Salvation of the sheep (after the Last Judgment).
(Thus) those are saved who are in the good of love and truths of faith from the Lord; and not those who are in proprium.
That the Lord is called the Son of Man, where it treats of Salvation, etc. Illustrated.
That... Jehovah took on the Human to save men. Illustrated.
It is from these things that the Lord is called Saviour and Redeemer.

For the Redeemer and Saviour of the world is no other than the Lord as to the Divine Human, which is called the Son. For Redemption and Salvation is an attribute proper to His Human, which is called merit and justice...
The spiritual sense of these words (concerning the 12 thousand sealed from every tribe) is that all with whom there is the Church from the Lord are saved. Explained.
Through the truths with a man, the Lord has the power of saving him...
Every man who has religion, knows... that he who lives well is saved, and that he who lives evilly is condemned. Explained.
Under Religion, see this reference.
(Such a priest) does a good work, because from he love of saving souls.
It is a common opinion that to be saved is to believe this or that...
That without Him no mortal could have been saved; and that they are saved who believe in Him. DFaith 35. DFaith 36. AR 67. BE 116. TCR 2. AE 806:end.
The Divine love wills to save all; but it cannot save except through the Divine wisdom; and to the Divine wisdom belong all the laws through which Salvation is effected.
The Lord permits (this) for the sake of the end, which is Salvation.
That the Divine Providence in everything... regards what is infinite and eternal from itself, especially in saving the human race. General article. DP 58.
(That man should be in this strong appearance) the Lord wills for the sake of his Salvation; for, without this appearance (that he does good, etc. as of himself) no one can be saved.
This is why evils do not damn a regenerated person, and goods do not save an unregenerated one.
All born men in any religion can be saved, provided they acknowledge God, and live according to the precepts which are in the decalogue. Explained. DP 254:2.
Confirms himself against the Divine Providence because (some) place salvation in certain words... Explained.
It is provided that everyone in every heresy... can be reformed and saved, provided he shuns evils as sins, and does not confirm the false heretical things...
That evils are permitted for the sake of the end, which is Salvation. General article. DP 281, Explained.
He says to himself. Is not this (Gentile) saved?... Can this (Christian) be saved?
That hence it is from the Divine Providence that every man can be saved; and that they are saved who acknowledge God, and live well. General article.
That these (two things) are the generals of all religions, through which everyone can be saved. Explained.
That the man himself is in fault, if he is not saved. General article.
That (in spite of the decrease and consummation of religion) it is provided by the Lord that everyone can be saved. Explained.
Also that all who die as infants, wherever born, are saved.
(Thus) no man lacks a Knowledge of the means through which he can be saved; nor the power, if he wants to be saved; from which it follows that all have been predestinated to Heaven. DP 330:4.

The reason some are not saved, is that the Divine love wills that man should feel in himself the happiness and bliss of Heaven... and this cannot be, unless it appears to man that he thinks and wills from himself...
That those only are saved who have been born within the Church, is an insane heresy. Explained.
That the operation of the Divine Providence to save man begins from his birth, and lasts to the end of his life, and afterwards to eternity, General article. DP 333, Explained.

But no more can be saved than want to be saved; and those want to be saved who acknowledge God, and are led by Him: and those do not want, who do not acknowledge God, and lead themselves: for these do not think about eternal life, and Salvation.
That instantaneous Salvation from immediate mercy is not possible. General article.
That faith concerning instantaneous Salvation from immediate mercy has been taken from the natural state of man. Explained.

That the doctrines of the Churches in the Christian world, interiorly regarded, are against instantaneous Salvation from immediate mercy; but still the external men of the Church maintain it. Explained.
That instantaneous Salvation from immediate mercy is the flying fire-serpent in the Church. General article.
That through a faith in instantaneous Salvation from pure and mere mercy, there is induced security of life. Explained. (And damnation is imputed to the Lord. DP 340:5, Explained.)
There are two essentials through which is effected conjunction with God, and thence Salvation: the acknowledgement of one God, and repentance of life...
I have the keys of Hell and of death = that He alone can save. AE 86.
Therefore He who rules (Heaven) necessarily rules (Hell); otherwise, man could not be saved. To he saved is to be brought out of Hell.
That (he who is reformed becomes spiritual and) will be saved. Signified.
That He alone has the omnipotence of saving. Signified.
Hence, he who acts well, and thinks well; that is, who lives well, and believes well, will be saved.
Place Salvation, not in amendment of life, but in certain words...
Therefore he who lives according to these things because they are Divine truths... is saved; but he who lives according to them only because they are civil and moral truths, is not saved...
Thou hast redeemed us to God in Thy blood () = Salvation through conjunction with Him.
Unless they immediately approach God the Saviour...
These loves cannot be removed, except by God the Saviour... and they cannot by God the Saviour, unless He is approached...
That they are saved who are in the Lord and the Lord in them... and that no others are saved than those who believe in Him. Illustrated.

Who cannot see... that the salvation of man is the continual operation of the Lord with man, from his first infancy to the last of his life; and that this is purely Divine, and never possible to any man...

The very advent of the Lord into the world was solely for the sake of man's Salvation. For the sake of this. He assumed the Human, removed the Hells, and glorified Himself, and put on omnipotence even in ultimates.

That Salvation and eternal life primarily consists in worshipping the Lord, and in living according to His precepts... because through these is effected conjunction with the Lord, and consociation with the Angels. Signified, Explained.

The nations which are saved shall walk in the light of it () = that all who are in the good of life, and believe in the Lord, will there live according to Divine truths, and will see them within themselves...
That this is necessary at the end of the Church, in order that some may be saved. Signified, Explained.
That of these, although they are polygamists, those are saved who acknowledge God, and, from religion, live according to the civil laws of justice. Explained.

(Thus) without the advent of the Lord into the world, no one could have been saved. It is the like at this day, and therefore unless the Lord comes into the world again in the Divine truth which is the Word, no one can be saved. TCR 3.
God is in the perpetual endeavour of regenerating and thus saving man; but He cannot effect it except as man prepares himself a receptacle...
But those who know nothing about the Lord... if they believe in one God, and live according to the precepts of their religion, are saved by their faith and life...
That without this Redemption no man could have been saved. General article.
That thus He might be acknowledged in the Heavens as the Saviour of both worlds...
The Divine virtue and operation proceeding from... the Lord God the Saviour.
See Holy Spirit.
That saving faith is in the Lord God the Saviour Jesus Christ. General article.
That the sum of faith is that he who lives well, and believes rightly, is saved by the Lord. General article.
As it is impossible for God to damn anyone who lives well, and believes rightly; so... it is impossible for God to save anyone who lives evilly, and thence believes falsely. Explained.
The esse of the faith of the New Church is... 2. Trust that he who lives well, and believes rightly, is saved by (the Lord God the Saviour Jesus Christ.)

Who does not see (it) from a certain interior perception... when he hears anyone say. He who lives well and believes rightly, is saved? And who does not reject (it)... when he hears it said that he who believes rightly, and does not live well, is also saved? Explained... So again, if... it is said that he who lives well, although he does not believe, is saved. (See Life.)
That... unless man removes evils in part by repentance, he remains in them, and (therefore) cannot be saved. General article.
The Lord is continually in the act... of saving man; and no one can be saved unless he is being regenerated. Illustrated. Therefore regeneration is the means of salvation.

So that He could afterwards be present with men... and save those who would live according to His precepts, consequently regenerate and save them; for those are saved a ho are regenerated... And, as regeneration and salvation make one, all can be saved... That without the Lord's advent no one could have been saved, is to be understood thus: that... no one could have been regenerated.
He thereby became the Saviour, etc. to eternity.
Still, everyone, according to his state, can be regenerated and saved.
All these (in the three Heavens) have been saved, but in different ways.
See Regenerate.
For men have not approached the Saviour Him self...
For there is not any nation in the whole world which cannot be saved, if it acknowledges God, and lives well...
That the rich and powerful... are saved equally with the low and poor.
People are saved from every religion, even those in the doctrine of faith alone, provided they live the life of faith...
Hence they believed that all can be saved, even those in Hell; but were told that they cannot, because they are not in freedom...
No one is saved through these things alone. From experience.
Few (Jews) are saved; for no others are saved than those who believe in the Lord.
Power, when predicated of the Lord, principally regards Salvation. Illustrated.
Those who receive Divine truth in good are saved; but those who receive it... not in good, are not saved. Explained.

It here treats of those who are saved, although they had been in falsities... For all are saved who are in the good of life according to the dogmas of their own religion, which they have believed to be truths, although they are not truths. Explained.
All those are saved who are let into temptations...

Their having been in the good of life according to their religion does indeed save; but it does not save so long as they are in falsities; and therefore after (death) the falsities with them are removed. The reason they cannot be saved before, is that good derives its essence from truths...
Think to be saved through knowledge alone. Signified.
I Will save them by their God Jehovah () = Salvation by the Lord...
For the Lord could not save those who had been of His Church, until the dragon... had been expelled...
(Thus such) cannot be saved, because they do not want to be reformed and regenerated...
The Salvation and consequent joy of those who become spiritual through the reception of Divine truth. Signified, Explained.
Under Redeem, see this reference. AE 806:4.
These therefore... cannot be saved.
Why is not every man saved? Explained.
Those (who are found to be able to resist evils) are saved; but those who cannot, are not saved. Explained.
(Thus) the Lord provides that every man can be saved.
Those within the Church who deny the Divine of the Lord... cannot be saved.
Without this (thought about God: that He is one, and that He is the Lord) no one can be saved.
No one can be received and saved unless he acknowledges the Divine of the Lord in His Human; and therefore He so often said, Believest thou that I can do this?
If a man, through combat against evils as sins, has acquired any spiritual, although very little, he is saved...
Redemption 8. 13. This Salvation is perpetual redemption. Trinity 10. 7.
Trinity. 10. That unless a New Church comes forth... no flesh can be saved.
To worship God the Saviour cannot be prohibited throughout Christendom...
Swedenborgianism, which is the worship of the Lord our Saviour.
